title: Canary Fallback Rehearsal — Rollout Playbook Notes (2026-03-25)
body:
Meeting date: 2026-03-25
Attendees: Jordan Alvarez (owner), Priya Natarajan (console UI), Ben Thompson (rollouts), Rae Kim (observability), Luca Moretti (sre)

Purpose:
- Run a focused rehearsal of the canary fallback playbook for UI rollouts that hit degraded performance under load. Validate steps, check analytics correlations, and exercise automatic and manual fallback paths.

Agenda:
1) Quick recap of the recent incident that motivated the rehearsal (p95 latency spike during 3/19 canary).
2) Walk through the playbook steps for automatic fallback and manual rollback.
3) Verify observability signals and dashboards we will rely on during a real event.
4) Run a dry-run on staging with synthetic traffic and confirm trace propagation.
5) Capture action items and follow-ups.

Notes and decisions:
- Root cause recap: memory pressure from specific transformer attention kernel on certain sequence lengths; caused KV cache thrash and occasional CPU fallback paths -> p95 spike. Related ticket: ROLL-401.
- Decided to keep automatic fallback enabled for small traffic percentages (<=10%) but tighten the circuit-breaker window. Current circuit config: fail_rate_threshold=5%, window=10m -> proposed change to window=3m for faster reaction during high-variance workloads.
- Fallback target: route to quantized model variant (redwood/gptx-small-q4_0) + reduced max_output_tokens to 256. Confirmed artifacts exist in model registry.
- Observability: alert OBS-732 will be the primary alerting rule for rollouts. Alert expression: p95_latency(route:console) > 500ms for 5m AND error_rate(route:console) > 1% for 3m. We agreed to add a secondary signal: tokens_per_sec drop >40% vs baseline.
- Tracing: must ensure trace_id and deployment_tag are present in console UI logs for 100% of canary requests. Priya flagged that UI currently samples traces at 10% — updated requirement: sample 100% for canary route.

Dry-run (staging) observations:
- Synthetic traffic generator (rollout-tester v0.9) replayed a 10k req burst over 6 minutes. We observed the canary variant hit the threshold at ~3:45 and automatic fallback behaved as expected, switching 8% of traffic to the fallback model.
- However, we lost deployment_tag on ~12% of logs coming from the frontend proxy (trace mismatch). This broke correlation in the analytics dashboard. Root cause: proxy header rewrite in edge config -> replicated in GHPR. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/589.
- Metrics latency aggregation had a 20s delay in metrics pipeline due to a misconfigured ETL checkpoint. The 20s amortized delay is tolerable for human ops but not for an automatic rollback window of 30s. We noted pipeline improvement is needed.

Action items (owner — due):
- Ben Thompson — reduce circuit-breaker window from 10m -> 3m and add a short cool-down period (5m) to avoid oscillation. Update rollout config and test in staging. (due 2026-03-29)
- Priya Natarajan — temporarily increase trace sampling to 100% for canary route and validate deployment_tag propagation end-to-end; follow-up with UI proxy team to fix header rewrite. (due 2026-03-27)
- Rae Kim — update OBS-732 to include tokens_per_sec delta as a secondary signal and add a dashboard tile for quick visual triage. (due 2026-03-28)
- Luca Moretti — investigate metrics ETL checkpoint and propose a fix to reduce pipeline latency below 5s for critical rollout metrics. (due 2026-04-02)
- Jordan Alvarez — write a short runbook amendment that documents the changed circuit-breaker behavior and post a short announcement to #console-rollouts Slack. (due 2026-03-30)

Unresolved questions / open risks:
- If a fallback model has lower quality for certain prompt shapes, how do we automatically route only low-risk prompts? (Idea: tag prompts by eval suite score and add a routing policy) — needs input from the research/evals team (owner: TBD).
- Is 100% trace sampling for canaries acceptable from a cost/ingest perspective for larger customers? Priya will draft an impact note for privacy/cost.
- The metrics pipeline fix could take longer than one sprint; need a temporary mitigation: expand manual monitoring during rollouts and increase safe canary delay to 10m until pipeline latency is fixed.

Follow-ups scheduled:
- Quick checkpoint 2026-03-27 11:00 (15m) to confirm proxy header fix + trace sampling.
- Full replay and canary test 2026-03-31 with increased synthetic load (20k req over 10m) to validate cooldown behavior.

Reference links and scratch notes:
- Incident writeup (internal): CONFLUENCE:Incident-3-19-memory-thrash
- Rollout ticket: JIRA:ROLL-401
- Observability ticket: JIRA:OBS-732
- PR for proxy header fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/589
- Playbook canonical page: CONFLUENCE:Canary-Fallback-Playbook-9876

Notes to self (informal):
- Remember to capture a short clip of the dashboard transitions during the 3/31 replay for onboarding docs.
- Consider adding a 'quality_fallback' flag on the request to let SDKs opt out of fallback model if they require strict fidelity (research to weigh in).
- We should run a partial canary where fallback only happens for non-function-calling routes as an intermediate safety net.

Status: draft — want to iterate after 3/27 checkpoint and then promote to playbook final once staging tests pass.
